2609.11505.title: Structural priors for data-efficient language learning
2609.11505.paper_summary: Efficient language learning requires methods to reduce the reliance on large data and computational resources. We investigate structural transfer: First training models on non-language data to induce useful priors for natural language. This approach is a form of weight initialization for multilingual language modeling. We evaluate transfer via next-token-prediction loss, weight shifts in the model, and downstream linguistic benchmarks. Several symbolic data types - notably music, probabilistic grammars, and cellular automata - yield lower language-modeling loss than random initialization. These gains coincide with smaller weight shifts during subsequent language training, suggesting that structural transfer positions models in a more favorable region of the parameter space. However, a lower loss does not translate consistently into better downstream linguistic performance, and transfer from non-language data is less efficient than additional language data. We conclude that non-language data can serve as a partial substitute for language data for the training objective of next-token prediction but does not reliably support broader linguistic generalization.
2609.11505.paper_summary_zh: 有效的語言學習需要減少對大量數據和計算資源的依賴的方法。<lb/>我們研究結構轉移：首先在非語言數據上訓練模型，以誘導對自然語言有用的先驗知識。<lb/>這種方法是一種多語言語言建模的權重初始化形式。<lb/>我們通過下一個標記預測損失、模型中的權重變化和下游語言基準來評估轉移。<lb/>幾種符號數據類型——特別是音樂、概率文法和細胞自動機——產生的語言建模損失低於隨機初始化。<lb/>這些增益與隨後語言訓練期間較小的權重變化相一致，這表明結構轉移將模型置於參數空間中更有利的位置。<lb/>然而，較低的損失並不總是能夠一致地轉化為更好的下游語言表現，且來自非語言數據的轉移效率低於額外的語言數據。<lb/>我們得出結論，非語言數據可以作為下一個標記預測訓練目標的語言數據的部分替代，但並不可靠地支持更廣泛的語言概括。
